To check the recoverable costs and the value-adding share of the renovation, detailed renovation cost statements are needed, as per VMWG Art. 14 Abs. 1 and 3.
To verify the justification for the rent increase, a statement detailing cost increases is necessary, as per VMWG Art. 12.
To understand the full communication regarding the rent increase and any related subsidies, all correspondence from the landlord is needed.

To verify the justification for the rent increase, the landlord must provide a detailed breakdown of any cost increases, as per VMWG Art. 20 Abs. 1.
To understand the full communication history regarding the rent increase and any related issues, all correspondence between the landlord and tenant is needed.

The previous net rent statement is essential to establish the basis for the tenant's request and to assess the change in rent.

requests.why: To assess the validity of the rent increase and the reclassification of ancillary costs, the official form used by the landlord is required.
To determine the legally binding previous net rent, a statement of previous rent is needed.
All correspondence between the landlord and tenant regarding the rent adjustment and ancillary costs is necessary to understand the communication history and any agreements made.
To verify the justification for the rent increase, documentation of cost increases or renovation costs is needed.
To assess whether the new rent is abusive, evidence of comparable rents in the area is required.
If the rent is indexed, the relevant index publication is needed to verify the adjustment.

requests.why: To determine if the rent increase notification complies with formal requirements, including the use of an official form and proper justification, as per OR Art. 269d Abs. 1 and VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 1.
To understand the full communication history regarding the rent adjustment and any related discussions about the reclassification of ancillary costs.
To verify the exact net and gross rent amounts paid previously and currently, and to establish a clear history of rent payments.
To ascertain the previously valid net rent and to compare it with the new proposed rent, which is crucial for assessing the validity of the rent increase.
To evaluate the justification for the rent increase based on cost increases, value-enhancing improvements, comparable rents, or index adjustments, as per OR Art. 269a and VMWG Art. 11, 12, 14, 16.

requests.why: The tenant needs the official rent increase form to verify the validity of the rent increase and to understand the reasons for the increase.
Correspondence between the landlord and tenant is needed to understand the communication regarding the renovation, rent increase, and any agreements or disagreements.
The tenant needs the final invoices and a detailed statement of renovation costs to assess if the rent increase is justified and not abusive.
The tenant needs a statement of cost increases to verify the justification for the rent increase, especially if it is based on increased costs.
The previous rent statement is needed to compare with the new rent and assess the extent of the increase.
These documents are needed to confirm the date of receipt of the rent increase notification, which is crucial for calculating the 30-day period to challenge the increase.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: To verify if the rent increase notification complies with formal requirements, including the use of an approved form and proper justification, as per OR Art. 269d Abs. 1 and VMWG Art. 19 Abs. 1.
To understand the full communication history between the parties regarding the renovation, rent increase, and any related discussions about project completion, costs, and subsidies.
To assess the justification for the rent increase based on renovation costs, including details on value-enhancing improvements and any received subsidies, as required by VMWG Art. 14.
To verify if the rent increase is justified by cost increases or additional services, as per OR Art. 269a lit. b and VMWG Art. 12.
To check if the rent increase is justified by changes in the reference interest rate, as per VMWG Art. 12a.
To determine if the rent increase is justified by inflation, specifically the national consumer price index, as per OR Art. 269b and VMWG Art. 16.
To evaluate if the new rent is within the range of local or customary rents for comparable properties, as per OR Art. 269a lit. a and VMWG Art. 11 Abs. 1.
